jobs.title: Mobile Mechanic
jobs.description:
Job Description

Join the RAC. Together, we’re going places. A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000 A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary to £44,385, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm , and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

As an RAC Mobile Mechanic in the Service, Maintenance and Repair division, you’ll bring expert vehicle maintenance and diagnostic skills directly to our customers, wherever they are. From driveways to office car parks, you’ll deliver first-class service without the constraints of a traditional garage. We’ll equip you for success from day one - with your own RAC van, fuel card, full uniform, essential tools, and diagnostic kit all provided.

Think independence, career progression, and real work-life balance - with a 40-hour week that keeps you moving and out of the same four walls. The RAC has been a trusted name for over 125 years, combining our heritage with bold innovation. Now’s the time to join a company that’s redefining roadside repair.

If you’re a skilled, practical mechanic looking to be part of something big, this is for you. No CV required when you apply – it's easier than ever to start your journey with us. As a Mobile Mechanic at RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile: Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime.

A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday–Saturday availability (8am–8pm), offers flexibility and stability Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000.

It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward. Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings. Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays.

We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments. Financial Security & Perks - pension scheme with up to 6.5% matched contributions alongside life assurance cover up to 4x salary (10x optional with flex benefits), designed to support you long-term. Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16, offering reassurance whenever you need it.

Extras That Make a Difference - access Orange Savings, our exclusive discount portal with deals across top retailers, holidays, tools, tech and more. After passing probation, you’ll automatically join our Colleague Share Scheme, giving you a stake in our collective success. Sound like your kind of role?

Here’s what we’re after: You're someone who gets people. This isn’t just spanners and engines—our mechanics are out there on driveways, chatting with customers, giving advice, and representing the RAC with pride. You’re not just in the RAC—you are the RAC.

Every fix, every chat, every driveway visit shows what we’re all about. You like mixing things up. Every day’s a little different—servicing, diagnostics, repairs, and checks.

But it doesn’t stop there: you’ll manage your stock, do your reporting, and keep those customer conversations flowing. You think on your feet. You’ll be trusted to think on your feet and make the right call for each customer.

Different fixes, different faces, new challenges every day. What you’ll need: Level 2 light vehicle maintenance qualification (or equivalent) At least 2 years' hands-on experience as a vehicle technician working with a range of light vehicles A full UK driving licence with fewer than 6 points We’re Orange Heroes At the RAC, we never stand still. With a legacy of over 125 years, it’s this restless drive for better that’s earned the trust of over 12.5 million members and it’s why we’re on a mission to be the UK’s number one motoring services provider.

That commitment to excellence isn’t just felt by our members, it’s echoed by our people too. With a 4.5-star rating on Glassdoor, our colleagues recognise the RAC as a place where ambition, support and authenticity come together. We’re all about progress powered by people.

As an equal opportunities employer, we welcome every background, champion every voice and back your growth every step of the way. At the RAC, individuality fuels innovation and you’re invited to bring your full self to it.

jobs.title: Customer Service Representative - Uncapped Commission
jobs.description:
Job Description

Full time : Permanent Address: The Strand, Swansea, SA1 2AB What’s in it for you • Competitive Salary: Starting at £26,116, rising to £26,738 after 8 months, plus an uncapped monthly commission scheme • Online GP: Access to a private GP 24/7 for you and your immediate family • Paid Carer’s Leave: Market-leading carers leave with up to 2 weeks off • Family Leave: Equalised maternity, paternity, and adoption leave – 18 weeks’ full pay and 8 weeks’ half pay in the first year. • Huge Discounts: Save on EE & BT products, including mobile and broadband. • Career Development: Ongoing support to help you grow your skills and develop • Season Ticket Travel Loan: Funds for your travel to and from work.

• Volunteering Days: Paid time off to give back to your local community. • Optional Private Healthcare and Dental: Protection for you and your family. About the role If you’re someone who puts customers at the heart of every decision, understanding their needs, and helping them find the right solution, then this could be the perfect role for you.

This is a fast-paced, rewarding role where your communication skills, ability to adapt, drive and determination will help you succeed – and where your results are recognised and rewarded. At EE, we’re harnessing the power of technology to bring people together and make life better. Join our Swansea Sales Team, and you’ll be right at the heart of it – speaking with customers over the phone, learning what matters most to them, building relationships, and matching them with the perfect EE products and services.

From the latest mobile tech to smart home solutions and insurance protection, every call is an opportunity to make a genuine difference. You’ll use your energy and ambition from similar roles where you’ve thrived, met goals, achieved targets, influenced others, or provided great service and you’ll already have the transferrable skills to shine here. You’ll take responsibility for delivering results and collaborate with your team to share ideas and celebrate success.

We’ll give you all the training, tools, and support you need to build your confidence and achieve your targets. We understand that life doesn’t always follow a set schedule, so we help our people work flexibly – for example, allowing you to plan your own breaks or bank time off to make sure you don’t miss the moments that matter most. Bring your energy, curiosity, and ambition – and we’ll match it with opportunity.

Join us at EE and turn your potential into performance. This a regulated role and is subject to a bankruptcy check in addition to our regular pre employment checks.

jobs.title: Children's Residential Support Worker
jobs.description:
Job Description

£34,274 - £40,640 assuming good attendance and up to 4 sleep ins per month Those huge small victories Working in our Children’s Homes means being a part of a young person’s day to day life. This means being there for the highest highs and lowest lows. Our support workers enable our young people to get their childhood back and create pathways to become well rounded adults – an incredibly rewarding role to have.

There will be challenges along the way but there will also be the smallest moments which feel like a huge small victory! Our homes accommodate young people with social, emotional and mental health needs, and our aim is to create the best possible outcome for the young people in our care. Our support workers are fulfilled by the idea of affecting even the smallest positive changes in our young people, so we celebrate the little things.

Check out this video on what life as a Children's Residential Support Worker is like. Get out what you put in You’ll take care of our young people day to day, making sure things run smoothly and creating lasting memories. This involves making sure they are up and ready for school, helping with homework, completing paperwork and planning activities.

Evenings and weekends are for fun, whether that’s playing on the Xbox, a game of football, having a film day or going go-karting – not a bad way to spend your day at work! Working here is never dull, and the work really matters. It’s about tapping into each young person’s needs, personality and potential - and guiding them toward a positive future.

What we do for you We know you’re going to do great things. For your hard work and commitment, we reward you with the best salary and benefits package in the care sector. With us, you’ll get to make a genuine difference to the lives of our young people – plus you’ll get: Salary: Base salary of £29,034 - £35,400 Bonuses: In addition to your base salary you’ll do up to 4 sleep ins per months, these are paid at £80 per sleep (approx.

£3,840 per year) and £1,400 Attendance Allowance – assuming good attendance, £2,000 Regional Allowance, £1,000 Welcome Bonus - on successful completion of probation & £1,000 Loyalty Bonus (after 12 months of employment ) Training: A full 4-week induction on our Care Academy Holiday: You’ll work hard at WG, so you’ll be rewarded with 7 weeks’ holiday Progression: If career development is your thing, most of our team leaders and managers have been promoted from within our group – plus you could join our ‘Aspire’ future managers programme Flexible benefits package: meaning you can increase/decrease your holiday allowance, pension and life insurance – check out our benefits here Wellbeing: a host of wellbeing tools and advice including employee assistance Medical cover so you can claim back the cost of things like an opticians or dentist appointment and a host of high-street discounts Meals provided while you’re at work Beautiful working environments with the very best facilities – check out our homes here A recommend a friend scheme that offers a £1,000 bonus every time Bring your whole-self to work Here at Witherslack Group, we celebrate everyone’s differences as that’s what makes us the best at what we do. Our young people come from all walks of life, diverse backgrounds and with different needs – and our workforce reflects that diversity, so that our teams can engage, encourage and inspire our young people to be themselves. You don’t need experience, but there are a few things we’ll be looking for from you: A ‘can do’ attitude – a team player who rolls up their sleeves to help others We genuinely care about our young people (and each other) so honesty and empathy is a must The resilience to be able to deal with challenging situations A full UK driving licence which you’ve held for at least 12 months If you don’t have a Level 3 Diploma in Residential Childcare (or equivalent), we’ll pay for you to study and support you every step of the way You’ll start life as a RSW by joining our ‘Care Academy’ – 4 weeks of off the job training with experienced WG professionals to help you feel confident and ready to support our young people.

Join the UK’s best special education and care provider At Witherslack Group, inclusion is part of who we are. We’re committed to creating an environment where everyone feels respected, valued and that they truly belong. As a specialist provider of education and care for children and young people with special educational needs, we understand the importance of embracing individuality and championing difference- especially when it comes to neurodiversity.

We celebrate diverse perspectives, lived experiences, and the unique strengths that each person brings to our community. We welcome applications from people of all backgrounds, identities, and abilities. We are proud to be recognised as an inclusive employer and are committed to making our recruitment and workplace practices inclusive and accessible.

If you need any adjustments to support you through the recruitment process or in the workplace, we’ll be there every step of the way. By building a diverse and inclusive team, we’re better able to support the children, young people and families we serve and ensure every member of our team can thrive, grow, and be their authentic self. The Witherslack Group is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of its young people.

This post is subject to an enhanced DBS check (we will cover the cost) and an online search. We are an equal opportunities employer welcoming applications from all sections of the community. For a full job description and person specification, please click here .

To view our ex-offenders policy please click here . Children’s Support Worker / Residential Support Worker / Care Worker / Career in Care / Working with Children / SEMH

jobs.title: Prison Support - HMP Stocken
jobs.description:
Job Description

Prison Support Role HMP Stocken £29,432 His Majesty’s Prison and Probation Service. An extraordinary job. Done by someone like you.

As an Operational Support Grade, you will play a key part in supporting the day-to-day running of a busy prison. You will be part of a supportive team doing all sorts of things – from security and searches at the gate, to managing deliveries, supervising visitors, and monitoring phone calls and CCTV. It’s a varied and active job involving tasks which combine some desk duties with more physical tasks such as lifting, carrying and walking to escort vehicles across the prison grounds.

Someone like you You don’t need any qualifications to do this job, but if you are a good communicator and can keep calm under pressure, this fast-paced role could be the start of a successful career for you. Helping to keep a prison running smoothly and safely you will have good judgement and common sense, and, above all, be a great team player. As an OSG, you will work a variety of shifts, including weekend and night shifts, to keep things running.

An extraordinary job In this unique career, you’ll have the opportunity to protect the public and make an impact on lives by supporting the important work happening daily in our prisons. Unlike our prison officers, your contact with prisoners is limited, although depending on the particular prison you may interact with prisoners occasionally. The OSG role will give you significant knowledge and experience of how a prison operates.

It can provide opportunities to move into other prison jobs, including opportunities to apply for the OSG to Prison Officer conversion scheme. What you can expect from us: You’ll be given great training and opportunities for progression and development. In addition to your base pay, you will receive: annual leave is 25 days on appointment and will increase to 30 days after 10 years’ service (calculated on a pro-rata basis) 9 days bank, public and privilege holidays access to a paid Level 2 apprenticeship in customer service access to the generous Civil Service pension scheme season ticket loans, retail discounts, an Employee Assistance Programme and a Cycle to Work scheme If this sounds like you, apply now.

Join the RAC as a Roadside Technician Join the team that keeps the UK moving. Start and finish on your driveway.

Demand-led shifts averaging 40 hours per week, with optional overtime available. What you’ll need: • A Level 2 light vehicle maintenance qualification (or equivalent), with at least 2 years' post-qualification technical, electrical, and diagnostic experience • A customer-focused approach • A full UK driving licence As a Roadside Technician within our Patrol division, you’ll deliver expert mechanical roadside repair, vehicle diagnostics, and emergency breakdown support across the UK. Whether it’s a flat battery, tyre change, or complex fault-finding, you’ll provide quick, confident solutions and reassurance when our members need it most.

You’ll start and end your day at home, tackling challenges head-on and making a real impact on the roadside - combining your technical expertise with outstanding member service. We’ll set you up for success from day one, with your own RAC van, fuel card, full uniform, essential tools, and diagnostic kit all provided. The RAC has been a trusted name for over 125 years, combining heritage with innovation.

If you're looking for a career in roadside automotive services that’s rewarding, fast-paced, and full of variety - this is it. No CV required when you apply – it's easier than ever to start your journey with us. You thrive on variety. One moment it’s fault diagnostics, the next it’s a flat tyre or battery - no two jobs are the same. You’ll be equipped and ready for every call-out, with the tools, tech, and support to get the job done.

A competitive base salary of £40,170, with on-target earnings of up to £52,000 A guaranteed overtime option to increase your base salary to £44,385, plus additional overtime and bonus opportunities 40 hours per week, with core hours from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm , and 1 in 4 Saturdays.

As an RAC Mobile Mechanic in the Service, Maintenance and Repair division, you’ll bring expert vehicle maintenance and diagnostic skills directly to our customers, wherever they are. From driveways to office car parks, you’ll deliver first-class service without the constraints of a traditional garage. We’ll equip you for success from day one - with your own RAC van, fuel card, full uniform, essential tools, and diagnostic kit all provided.

The RAC has been a trusted name for over 125 years, combining our heritage with bold innovation. Now’s the time to join a company that’s redefining roadside repair.

If you’re a skilled, practical mechanic looking to be part of something big, this is for you. No CV required when you apply – it's easier than ever to start your journey with us. As a Mobile Mechanic at RAC, you’ll get benefits that go the extra mile: Earnings That Motivate - enjoy a market-competitive base salary of £40,170, with the opportunity to increase your earnings up to £52,000 through bonuses and premium-rate overtime.

A full-time 40-hour week, with Monday–Saturday availability (8am–8pm), offers flexibility and stability Opt-in Guaranteed Overtime - after your first month, you can choose to work extra rest days at £30 per hour. Just one extra day a month could earn you £3,000 more per year on top of your base salary. Two extra days could give you an extra £5,000.

It's your choice - more flexibility, more reward. Tools to Drive Your Future - get started with a free RAC Ultimate Complete Breakdown Service from day one, plus access to a car salary sacrifice scheme (including electric vehicle options) after 12 months, delivering serious tax savings. Time Off That Matters - enjoy 23 days of holiday (rising to 25 with service), plus bank holidays.

We also support work-life balance with paid family leave, flexible schedules, and practical resources to help navigate personal commitments. Wellbeing That Works for You - our 24/7 confidential support service is available to you and household members aged 16, offering reassurance whenever you need it.

Job Description

About the Role:

Grade Level (for internal use):
10

The Team: United Kingdom, Ireland and Netherlands C&RS Sales Team for Financial Institutions, is focused on selling the S&P Global Market Intelligence flagship solutions (RatingsDirect, RatingsXpress, CreditPro, Credit Analytics, and Scorecards) in the wide Financial Institution space in the United Kingdom, Ireland and Netherlands.

We are looking for an addition to our London or Amsterdam office-based C&RS Sales Specialists Team who will be selling our market leading Solutions to existing and new customers.

As a Sales Specialist responsibilities will include:
  • Providing the best possible service to existing and potential new customers
  • Build, execute and identify opportunities for growth
  • Meet or exceed your individual growth goal / quota
  • Planning and executing of sales campaigns.
  • Adopt structured and disciplined approach to tracking activity, pipeline accuracy and forecasting"
  • Identify and develop revenue synergy and cross-sell opportunities""
  • Build and maintain a knowledge of current industry and economic events impacting our clients and the relevance of our products.
  • Partner closely with your direct team members and other internal stakeholders such as Product Experts, Product Management, Marketing, Legal and Client support teams."
Facts/Possibilities:
  • Meritocratic Team setup with corresponding career and earning possibilities
  • Being part of an innovative high growth business line
  • A team with a good mixture of relatively new and long-term S&P employees
Basic Required Qualifications:
  • Minimum of three years relevant sales experience.
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree or an additional equivalent of relevant work experience
  • Fluent in English
  • Prior experience in selling Market Data to Financial Institutions is an advantage
  • Knowledge of Credit Risk and fixed income markets is an advantage
Right to Work Requirements:

jobs.description:
Job Description

Telemetry Architect
Remote Working

£800 - £900pd
 

We are looking for someone to design and implement an observability model for a bank’s payments platform, leveraging Dynatrace and OpenTelemetry to improve infrastructure and application monitoring while reducing alert noise. Enhance business service–level observability by developing scalable approaches for transaction tracking, health indicators, and near real-time visibility across the end-to-end payments processing lifecycle.

 

emagine is a high-end professional services consultancy and solutions firm Specialising in providing business and technology services to the financial services sector, we power progress, solve challenges and deliver real results through tailored high-end consulting services and solutions.

 

We have created a culture of openness and integrity by building genuine and strong relationships and partnerships, enabling us to be uncompromising in our dedication in delivering the optimal service for our clients. Our commitment is not just towards our clients but we aim to foster a positive and equitable working environment with our consultants and colleagues which stems from our core values: Confident, Dedicated, Responsible, Genuine.

 

Responsibilities

 

  • Architect a collision-free environment by defining standards for Dynatrace and OpenTelemetry coexistence, including collector configurations and agent prioritization.

  • Build infrastructure observability frameworks with advanced, noise-free metrics (e.g., latency-based health indicators) and AI-enhanced alerting systems.

  • Develop multi-model approaches for application/business service observability, incorporating transaction volume trending, real-time message reconciliation, and topology-aware monitoring for diverse services.

  • Leverage OpenTelemetry for instrumentation in custom applications and Dynatrace for aggregation, shifting from SQL-based views to tool-driven dashboards and APIs.

  • Lead maturity assessments, proof-of-concepts, and roadmap planning to evolve observability across the organization.

 

Must Haves

 

  • 5+ years in observability architecture, with deep expertise in OpenTelemetry (e.g., semantic conventions, exporters) and Dynatrace (e.g., PurePath tracing, service modeling).

  • Strong understanding of distributed systems, microservices, and business process monitoring in financial or transaction-heavy environments.

  • Proficiency in infrastructure metrics (MQ, JVM, threads) and tools for data visualization (e.g., Grafana integration).

  • Experience with cloud-native technologies (Kubernetes, AWS/Azure) and scripting for automation.

  • Advanced degree in IT or Engineering; certifications in observability tools or cloud architecture.

 

Nice to Haves

 

* Familiarity with AI-enhanced monitoring techniques.

* Experience in leading observability transformation initiatives.

* Understanding of Agile methodologies in observability architecture.

Job Description

CAD Manager – MEP Design

We are seeking a talented and proactive CAD Manager to take a leading role in the production and coordination of MEP designs across a wide range of projects — from small-scale refurbishments to large residential, education, and commercial developments. This is an exciting opportunity for a driven CAD professional with a strong eye for detail who values technical excellence, collaboration, and the satisfaction of delivering high-quality design outputs.

As CAD Manager, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring drawings, models, and design information meet the highest technical and quality standards. You will work closely with engineers and remote teams to deliver coordinated, accurate, and timely outputs that support successful project delivery.

Key Responsibilities


Drawing Production & Coordination

  • Produce accurate, coordinated 2D MEP drawings up to construction level.
  • Translate engineers’ mark-ups and briefs into clear, high-quality CAD drawings.
  • Manage MEP drawings, models, worksets, and sheets to project standards.
  • Ensure effective coordination across MEP, architectural, and structural disciplines.


Team Leadership & Collaboration

  • Liaise daily with engineers to understand project deadlines and incoming CAD requests.

  • Undertake hands-on CAD production alongside management responsibilities.
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to CAD technicians.
  • Support engineers at design team and client meetings, contributing to coordination and technical discussions.


Quality, Standards & Process

  • Follow and enhance QA and BIM processes in line with industry standards.
  • Maintain compliance with Building Regulations, British Standards, and industry best practice (CIBSE, BSRIA, UK BIM Framework, ISO 19650).
  • Ensure drawings and models are stored and managed in accordance with document control and digital engineering procedures.
  • Manage document issue sheets and published drawing outputs for each project.


Skills & Experience Required

  • 5–10 years’ proven experience producing MEP drawings using AutoCAD.
  • Strong understanding of building services, coordination, and construction processes.
  • Experience working within a small to medium-sized consulting engineering environment.
  • Proven ability to manage drawing production across multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Confident setting up and managing 2D layouts, schematic drawings, and MEP models.
  • Excellent communication and organisational skills with strong attention to detail.
  • Commercial awareness and understanding of project delivery.
  • Knowledge of Building Regulations, CDM Regulations, and British Standards.
  • Collaborative mindset with the ability to work across teams and disciplines.


Software Skills

  • AutoCAD – Essential
  • Revit – Preferred
  • Navisworks – Preferred
  • Microsoft Excel / Word – Essential
  • IES – Desirable


Why This Role Matters


This role is central to the design delivery process — ensuring every drawing, model, and coordination effort meets the technical precision and professional standards clients expect.

Your leadership in maintaining drawing quality, managing information flow, and mentoring others will directly influence efficiency, reputation, and overall project success.

jobs.title: Graduate / Early Career Air Quality Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

We are currently looking for newly qualified or early career Air Quality Consultant to join our growing team.


DustScanAQ is a small, independent, employee-owned environmental consultancy firm based in Oxfordshire that specialises in dust and air quality monitoring, consultancy and assessment.


As we're an employee owned business (EOB), full-time employees also become co-owners, beneficiaries of the DustScan Trust and eligible for equal profit shares.


Our consultancy team undertake a range of expert dust, air quality and odour assessments typically for planners, developers, energy and mineral sector clients. A key part of your role will be supporting the delivery of assessments using a range of predictive models. Site work may occasionally be required; this will typically involve undertaking inspections and reviews of site processes, as well as installing air quality monitoring equipment. Our work ranges from one-off assessments to complex on-going expert witness cases. Support work includes assisting in project management, preparing quotes, and management of routine data collection and analysis.


We are currently looking for a new consultant to specifically assist with climate change assessments, dust and air quality impact assessments, ADMS Roads and ADMS point source modelling to support planning applications. Applicants will ideally already have some consultancy experience, but newly qualified candidates will also be considered.


The ideal applicant should have a 2.1 in a relevant Master’s or Bachelor’s degree, such as Environmental Science, Geography or Air Pollution Management, and should have a keen interest in environmental and air quality issues. Prior experience in a consultancy role (inc. placements/internships) is desirable, but full training will be provided.


The successful applicant may be required to assist in other areas of the business as required, such as with dust characterisation analysis and reporting including microscopy.


The position is mainly desk/office based in Witney (Oxfordshire, UK), with future potential for hybrid working. You must be prepared to commute to our offices.


Applicants must be eligible to work in the UK and a full UK driving license is desirable.


As we’re a small, specialist environmental consultancy we also value individuals who develop an interest in all aspects of our business and understand both the spirit and responsibility of employee-ownership.


Our core values are collaboration, professionalism and the application of scientific rigour. As an EOB we are motivated by our collective success, development and wellbeing. We strive for a culture of transparency, diversity and respect for all. As environmental consultants we are acutely aware of our need to operate sustainably, ethically and responsibly.


Requirements:


Education and Experience


  • A relevant Bachelor’s or Master’s degree (minimum 2:1), such as Environmental Science, Geography, Air Pollution Management etc.
  • Prior experience in a consultancy role (e.g. placement/internship) is desirable but not essential; all training will be provided.


Language and Technical Skills


  • Good command of written and spoken English and have a high standard of technical report writing
  • Proficient in the use of Microsoft Office, in particular Word and Excel
  • Preferably experience carrying out complex data routines, using GIS software and an understanding of air quality dispersion modelling using ADMS Roads. Full training will be given.
  • Experience in Python or R
  • Experience undertaking site/client-facing work is desirable but not necessary
  • Friendly and courteous telephone manner


Other


  • UK permit to work
  • Full UK driving license (or working towards a full license)


Desirable personal attributes:


We are looking for a team player who is driven and able to prioritise their workloads to meet tight deadlines whilst maintaining a high professional standard.


  • Happy working in a team environment and have the confidence to work under pressure to deadlines
  • A keen interest in environmental matters
  • A holistic approach to problem-solving
  • Resilient and able to deal with ambiguity
  • Be a strategic and analytical thinker
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Relevant technical knowledge
  • Both non-relevant and relevant work experience (e.g. through internships) would be advantageous
  • Willing to travel and stay away from home when required


Benefits of joining DustScanAQ:


  • Joining a growing EOB – you will become a co-owner and beneficiary of the DustScan Trust after your probationary period
  • EOB profit shares
  • Support to join professional bodies, such as the Institution of Environmental Science (IES), Institute of Air Quality Management (IAQM) and Institute of Sustainability and Environmental Professionals (ISEP)
  • Competitive salary, 7% pension contribution and benefits including private health insurance and dental care
  • 25 days annual leave + bank holidays, with additional leave awarded to recognise long-service
  • Corporate volunteering policy
  • Octopus EV company car scheme (subject to availability)
  • Working within a small, friendly team with a good learning environment


Location: Witney, Oxfordshire (office-based). Occasional site work throughout the UK

Contract: Permanent. Flexibility for home working once suitably experienced

Hours: Full-time, typically 09:00 - 17:00 (Mon-Fri)

Salary: £25,000 – £35,000 depending on experience

Start Date: Flexible, but ideally as soon as possible.

If you’re looking to develop a long-term career in recruitment within a supportive, high-performance environment, we’d welcome your application.

Candidate Profile

jobs.title: Clinical Rater
jobs.description:
Job Description

Clinical Rater

Full time/ Part time.


Who are we?

Clerkenwell Health is a pioneering mental health research organisation specialising in psychedelic-assisted therapy. We conduct innovative, scientifically grounded clinical trials through our integrated Contract Research Organisation (CRO), broad Clinical Research Facility (CRF) network, and Therapist Training Programme. We have also expanded our focus to the treatment of central nervous system (CNS) disorders, in addition to complex mental health conditions.


The Role

We’re looking for a Clinical Trials Psychologist/Rater who will support the delivery of Phase 1–3 clinical trials, to ensure high-quality patient care and adherence to Sponsor requirements, ICH-GCP, and relevant regulatory standards. The role is central to studies involving psychedelic compounds, mental health, neuropsychiatric disorders, and future therapeutic areas, with a strong focus on the timely and ethical conduct of clinical research.


This position combines hands-on clinical research responsibilities with direct participant interaction, including validated psychiatric and neurological assessments, supporting dosing sessions, and collecting high-quality clinical data. You will provide leadership within the research team, collaborate cross-functionally, and maintain the highest standards of participant safety, protocol compliance, and data integrity in complex and sensitive research environments.


Key responsibilities include:

  • Conduct structured and semi-structured psychiatric and neuropsychiatric assessments, including but not limited to: MADRS, MINI, CGI-S / CGI-I & HAM-A.
  • Conduct participant screening, eligibility assessments, baseline evaluations and outcome measurements following study protocols, regulatory approvals, and GCP guidelines.
  • Identify, document and escalate adverse events. Provide session oversight, including real-time clinical decision-making and adverse event management.
  • If appropriate, taking informed consent, performing concomitant Medication assessment, Physical examinations, medical history, etc
  • Where possible, support dosing sessions as a dosing session monitor (lead or assistant DSM or facilitator during clinical sessions, ensuring participant safety and adherence to the protocol.
  • Act as a key site/scientific representative during sponsor reviews, CRO oversight, audits, and regulatory inspections (e.g., MHRA, FDA).
  • Ensure clinical data quality, accurate source documentation standards per ALCOA++ principle and endpoint reliability.
  • Support staff induction, onboarding, and ongoing training in clinical assessments, study procedures, and GCP compliance.


Essential Experience & Qualifications

  • Advanced degree or equivalent experience in Psychology, Neuroscience, Pharmacology, Biomedical Science, Medicine or related field.
  • Significant experience delivering interventional CNS, psychedelic, psychopharmacology or mental health clinical trials in commercial or regulated environments.
  • Demonstrated competence in psychiatric assessments (MADRS, MINI, CGI, HAM-A).
  • Strong working knowledge of GCP and relevant regulatory guidelines


Is this the role for you?

At Clerkenwell Health, our core values are Compassion, Collaboration, Innovation, and Integrity. If you're excited about contributing to pioneering psychedelic and mental health research, and you’re passionate about delivering safe, ethical, and evidence-based therapy, we’d love to hear from you.

We are working with a fast-growing data and AI consulting business helping organisations understand and deploy modern AI capabilities in real operational environments.

As part of the next stage of growth, the firm is looking to hire a Generative & Agentic AI Strategy Lead who can help shape how organisations adopt and deploy large language models, generative AI systems, and emerging agentic architectures.

You will help organisations understand how modern AI systems actually work, where they create value, and how they can be implemented responsibly and effectively.


This includes shaping initiatives involving:


  • Large Language Models (LLMs)

  • Agentic AI systems and multi-agent architectures
  • AI-assisted decision systems
  • Generative AI applications embedded within enterprise workflows


You will work across the full lifecycle of AI initiatives — from early strategic conversations and concept development through to proof-of-concept, MVP delivery, and real operational deployment.

AI Strategy & Advisory

Evangelism & Thought Leadership

What We’re Looking For

This role requires someone who combines technical credibility with consulting polish.

The successful candidate will be comfortable:

  • Speaking in rooms with deep technical specialists

  • Bridging the gap between concept, architecture, and real-world delivery

About the Role



The Construction Manager will be responsible for ensuring that construction activities are completed on schedule, within budget and in compliance with safety and quality standards.

  • Site Management & Coordination

    15+ years of experience in the Chemical, FMCG, Manufacturing industries, Warehouse or EPC with a strong background in mechanical, piping, civil, structural & electrical construction management.

jobs.title: Multiple Remote Architectural Opportunities - Architectural Assistants up to Senior Architect level
jobs.description:
Job Description

A Different Way to Practice Architecture...


Multiple Remote Architectural Opportunities (Architectural Assistants up to Senior Architect level)


International Design Studio (Remote Collaboration Model)



Not every architect thrives in a busy studio environment.


Some do their best thinking when they have space… space to focus, space to design, and space to work deeply without the noise and distraction that often comes with large offices.


For the right individuals, this opportunity offers a very different way of practicing architecture.


About the Studio…


We are working with a highly experienced architectural design leader who runs a boutique international design consultancy operating across architecture, design advisory and strategic project input.


Earlier in his career he was a key figure within one of the UK’s well-known architectural studios, helping lead a respected team delivering a range of projects including residential, hospitality and mixed-use schemes across the UK and internationally.


Today, the studio operates with a deliberately different structure.


Rather than building a large permanent office team, the practice collaborates with a carefully curated network of architects and designers working remotely, assembling teams around specific projects. The studio sometimes describes this approach as building an “Avengers-like” collective of architectural professionals, each bringing their own specialist skills, interests and perspectives to the work.


It is a model that allows talented individuals to contribute to exceptional projects internationally, while maintaining the flexibility and focus that traditional studio environments rarely offer.


Current Opportunities…


The studio is currently supporting a large and varied portfolio of live projects internationally, resulting in the need to expand their network of collaborating architects.


They are therefore keen to identify architectural professionals across several levels:


  • Part 1 Architectural Assistants
  • Part 2 Architectural Assistants
  • Architects
  • Senior Architects / Senior Designers


In particular, the studio would be very interested in speaking with experienced architects or senior designers who are confident shaping projects at concept and planning stages, helping lead early design thinking on a number of live schemes.


Projects span both UK-based and international work, covering a varied range of scales and typologies including high-end residential developments, hospitality projects, boutique resort concepts and mixed-use schemes.


The studio’s work ranges from smaller, design-led private developments through to large-scale international projects, often forming part of wider masterplans or complex multi-building schemes.


Much of the studio’s work sits at the early design and planning stages, where strong architectural thinking, creativity and the ability to shape a project from first principles are particularly valued.


That said, there are also opportunities for architectural professionals who enjoy developing projects technically, supporting the progression of live schemes through detailed design and delivery stages where required.


One of the strengths of this working model is that architects are often matched to projects based on their particular strengths and interests, whether that be early-stage design thinking, strategic concept development, sector specific or technical delivery.


Fully Remote Working…


All roles operate completely remotely.


Architects collaborate through daily virtual check-ins and ongoing project coordination, working together across different locations and time zones.


Architects collaborating with the studio do so on a contractor basis, typically operating through their own limited company.


This model tends to work particularly well for individuals who:


  • are comfortable working independently
  • enjoy extended periods of focused design work
  • have a well-organised home working environment
  • communicate clearly and thoughtfully
  • prefer depth of work over constant studio activity


Many of the architects who thrive most within this structure describe themselves as naturally more introverted or reflective in their working style.


This is a focused, design-led working environment rather than a traditional busy studio culture.


Contractor Model…


As mentioned, architectural professionals joining the studio collaborate on a contractor basis, typically operating through their own limited company.


This arrangement allows the studio to work with talented individuals regardless of their physical location, while also offering a level of flexibility that many architects increasingly value.


Importantly, this is not a short-term or experimental model.


We originally introduced architects to the studio over five years ago under this structure, and several of those individuals are still working with the practice today.


For the right person, this can therefore become a long-term and stable collaboration.


At the same time, the model can also suit individuals who may want a defined period of experience before moving on.


For example:


  • Part 1 or Part 2 architectural assistants planning to return to university
  • architects seeking greater lifestyle flexibility
  • experienced designers looking for long-term remote work


Software Environment…


The studio takes a flexible approach to software, with projects currently utilising a combination of:


  • Revit
  • AutoCAD
  • Vectorworks


Different projects may require different platforms, but overall the focus is on capability rather than strict software alignment.


Exposure to Both UK and Global Projects…


Architects working with the studio gain exposure to an unusually diverse range of work.


Current and recent projects include:


  • luxury residential developments
  • boutique hospitality schemes
  • island resort masterplans
  • private client developments
  • residential and mixed-use projects in major international markets


Who This Might Suit…


This opportunity will not appeal to everyone.


But it tends to resonate strongly with architectural professionals who:


  • enjoy working independently and thoughtfully
  • are comfortable with fully remote collaboration
  • value focus and autonomy
  • are excited by international projects and varied design challenges
  • want to contribute to a design-led global project portfolio, whilst still having the opportunity to work on UK projects.


This is a rare opportunity to collaborate with a highly experienced design leader on ambitious projects around the world, within a working model that prioritises focus, flexibility and creativity.


As mentioned, opportunities exist across multiple levels, from Part 1 Architectural Assistants through to Senior Architects, and we are open to speaking with individuals who feel this style of working may suit them.


If this sounds like something you would enjoy exploring, please apply with your CV, respond to our screening questions and we will be in touch shortly.

jobs.title: Assistant Lecturer (with Mentorship)
jobs.description:
Job Description

Assistant Lecturer (with Mentorship)

Department: Academic
Locations: Derby
Position Type: Permanent
Working Hours: 37.5 hours per week
Working Pattern: Monday to Friday/ 9am to 5pm/ 5
days in the office
Salary: £30,000 - £35,000 per
annum depending on experience
Reports to: Course Director
Works closely with: Course Director, Lecturers,
Senior Lecturers, Personal Academic Tutors (PATs), Senior PATs, Wellbeing
Officers, Office Heads, Heads of Academics

Job Description

Assistant Lecturers are early-career or developing academics
who contribute to teaching and student support under structured mentorship and
supervision. The role is designed to build teaching capability, confidence, and
professional identity, supporting progression to Lecturer level.

Assistant Lecturers do not hold full accountability for
modules, assessment outcomes, or quality assurance. Instead, they develop their
practice through co-teaching or supported full teaching responsibilities,
supported assessment activity, and guided engagement with UKMC academic
frameworks and professional standards.

Role Delivery Focus (PFF/PFD)

The primary focus of this role is the delivery of Preparing
for Foundation (PFF) and Preparing for Degree (PFD) provision.

Assistant Lecturers will deliver most of their teaching
within PFF and PFD timetabled sessions, supporting students in developing
academic skills, confidence, English proficiency, and readiness for higher
education study.

They will work closely with Quality and Compliance
colleagues, as well as assessment delivery officers, to ensure alignment with
institutional frameworks, including the Inclusive Curriculum Framework (ICF),
English Proficiency Framework (EPF), and SEBAC.

They will collaborate with Admissions teams to support
transition points into programmes, ensuring coherence between pre-entry,
onboarding, and early-stage academic development.

They will be coordinated under a Lead for PFF/PFD, who
provides academic direction, consistency of delivery, and alignment across
campuses.

They may also provide occasional lecture or seminar cover
within their subject specialism, where appropriate, to support programme
delivery and further develop disciplinary teaching experience.

This delivery model ensures meaningful contribution to
student success, continuation, and belonging, while enabling development within
a structured and supported environment.

Job Responsibilities

 

Teaching, Learning and Curriculum (Supported)

·        
Deliver small-group tutorials, lectures,
workshops, and seminars under the guidance of a Lecturer or Senior Lecturer.

·        
Co-teach selected lectures with experienced
colleagues to build teaching confidence and effectiveness.

·        
Support the preparation and delivery of learning
activities aligned to approved module materials and learning outcomes.

·        
Prepare and maintain learning materials and
activities on the Virtual Learning Environment (VLE) under supervision.

·        
Apply inclusive teaching practices that support
student engagement, belonging, and continuation.

 

Assessment and Academic Practice (Supervised)

·        
Undertake first marking, second marking, and
moderation activities under guidance, ensuring alignment with assessment
criteria and regulations.

·        
Support the promotion of assessment literacy and
academic integrity.

·        
Develop understanding of assessment standards,
feedback practices, and moderation processes.

·        
Escalate assessment concerns promptly to module
teaching teams and mentors.

 

Student Support, Engagement and Attendance

·        
Monitor student engagement and attendance
through teaching sessions and the VLE, reporting concerns promptly.

·        
Support academic development through tutorials,
workshops, and formative feedback.

·        
Work collaboratively with PATs, Wellbeing
Officers, and academic services to ensure integrated student support.

·        
Develop awareness of referral pathways and
escalation processes.

 

Student Voice and Reflective Practice

·        
Engage with student feedback and adapt teaching
approaches with mentor guidance.

·        
Contribute to “you said, we did” feedback
processes at session level.

·        
Develop reflective teaching practice through
observation, feedback, and mentorship dialogue.

 

Professional Development, Mentorship and Framework
Learning

·        
Engage in a structured mentorship programme with
a Lecturer or Senior Lecturer.

·        
Maintain reflective practice logs aligned to
professional standards such as the PSF.

·        
Participate in peer observation cycles as both
observer and observed.

·        
Develop understanding of UKMC frameworks,
including ICF, EPF, SEBAC, and the Career-Ready Framework (CRF).

·        
Work towards professional recognition such as
Associate Fellowship of Advance HE or a PGCert in Higher Education.

·        
Contribute to curriculum enhancement or
employability initiatives where appropriate.

 

Professional Conduct and Collaboration

·        
Work collaboratively with teaching teams, PATs,
Wellbeing, and academic services.

·        
Participate in meetings, training, and
development activities.

·        
Promote and adhere to Equal Opportunities
policies and professional standards of conduct.

 

Essential Criteria

·        
A degree in a relevant discipline or equivalent
professional or industry experience.

·        
Demonstrated subject knowledge and ability to
support student learning in higher education.

·        
Commitment to developing teaching practice
through mentorship and reflective practice.

·        
Understanding of inclusive teaching practices
and their impact on student engagement and progression.

·        
Strong communication and interpersonal skills
for small-group and tutorial teaching.

·        
Willingness to work towards Associate Fellowship
of Advance HE or equivalent accreditation.

Desirable Criteria

·        
Previous teaching, tutoring, or mentoring
experience in higher or further education.

·        
Familiarity with Virtual Learning Environments
such as Moodle, Blackboard, or Canvas.

·        
Experience supporting diverse student cohorts,
including those with additional learning or language needs.

·        
Experience supporting assessment literacy or
academic integrity.

·        
Interest in curriculum innovation, employability
initiatives, or pedagogic research.

·        
Evidence of reflective practice or engagement
with professional learning.

 

KPI Framework – Assistant Lecturer (with Mentorship)

·        
Teaching Development and Mentorship: Completion
of structured mentorship plan, reflective logs, peer observations, and
development activities – target 100%.

·        
Assessment Practice (Supervised): Completion of
marking and moderation tasks under guidance, demonstrating developing
assessment literacy and integrity – target 100%.

·        
Inclusive Teaching and Belonging: Student
feedback evidencing inclusive practice, belonging, and confidence – target ≥75%
belonging and ≥70% confidence.

·        
Engagement Monitoring and Reporting: Active use
of VLE and timely escalation of student concerns – target 100% compliance.

·        
Collaboration and Employability Contribution:
Positive mentor feedback and contribution to at least one curriculum or
employability activity annually – target ≥90% mentor feedback and at least one
contribution.

·        
Professional Framework Development: Engagement
with ICF, EPF, SEBAC, CRF, and PSF through reflection and development planning
– target 100% participation.

 Benefits


  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Opportunities for professional development and career progression.
  • Access to academic resources and support networks.
  • Supportive and inclusive academic community.

Job Description

Job Title: Building Documentation Specialist

Start Date: ASAP

Duration: 3–6 months (potential to extend)

Pay Rate: £19–£25 per hour

Hours: Monday–Friday, 40 hours per week (8am–5pm)

Location: Soho, London

Working Pattern: Hybrid — 3 days in the office, 2 days from home

Travel: Regular visits to London clubs, sites, and venues within the estate


Overview

We are seeking a highly organised and detail-focused Technical Documentation Coordinator to take ownership of developing clear, accurate and user‑friendly Building User Guides (BUGs) across a luxury hospitality estate. This role involves reviewing technical information, validating service locations, and transforming complex building details into simple, accessible documentation for operational teams. This is an admin-heavy, research-driven role ideal for someone who thrives on coordination, information gathering, and producing consistent, polished documents. You will work closely with internal teams, external contractors, and subject matter experts to ensure that all building information is complete, reliable, and aligned with brand standards.


Key Responsibilities

  • Review existing as‑built documentation to identify, verify, and map mechanical, architectural, and MEP service locations.
  • Research, source, and clarify technical information from various internal and external stakeholders.
  • Develop, structure, and complete Building User Guide templates for multiple sites across the estate.
  • Translate complex technical details into clear, user-friendly language suitable for non-technical readers.
  • Maintain consistent formatting, branding, and technical standards across all documents.
  • Track progress, outstanding information, and dependencies across multiple simultaneous documents.
  • Identify gaps, inconsistencies, or discrepancies in existing documentation and coordinate with relevant teams to resolve them.
  • Work onsite across London clubs and venues to validate layouts, record information, and confirm service locations where needed.

jobs.title: Recruitment Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description

About the job


Who We Are

Frame 25 is a specialist recruitment business at the centre of the broadcast, media and technology industries. Our clients include national news broadcasters, sports rights holders, streaming platforms, post-production facilities and the technology businesses that keep them all on air.


We place technical and commercial talent from entry-level through to executive, across both permanent and freelance markets.


We’re hiring a consultant who wants to build a career in one of the most fast-moving and high-impact areas of media: live broadcast, streaming and production technology.


The Role

We’re looking for someone sharp, personable and genuinely motivated to build a long-term career in a specialist market.

This role suits someone with 1–3 years’ experience in a customer-facing, sales or service environment who wants to step into a more relationship-led, high-value recruitment model.

You’ll work closely with senior consultants on live assignments, developing your understanding of the industry while playing a real part in delivering for clients and candidates.

Recruitment here isn’t about firing out CVs. It’s about understanding what a customer actually needs, finding the right people for it, and building relationships that last beyond a single placement.

You’ll have real visibility and responsibility from early on - this isn’t a role where you’ll be one of many.


A Typical Day

Your morning might start with a briefing call alongside a senior consultant. A broadcaster is launching a new live sports programme and needs to build the technical crew from scratch: a team of engineers, operators and production staff, all starting within the same two-week window.

Your job is to understand the brief properly, get into the candidate market quickly, and start identifying the right people.

From there, you might be screening candidates, having conversations that go beyond the CV, writing up a shortlist with proper assessment behind it rather than just a list of names, and keeping the client updated with useful insight.

Later in the day, you might be researching a new area of the market, tracking down a specialist in a niche technical role, or supporting a senior consultant with a retained search for a more senior hire.

No two days look the same - which is either something that appeals to you or it isn’t.


What We’re Looking For

At least 1–3 years in a customer-facing, sales or service role. We’re less focused on the sector than on whether you can demonstrate the right behaviours.

Someone who communicates clearly and builds rapport naturally. A lot of the people we work with are highly experienced specialists - being credible with them matters from day one.

Organised and self-motivated. Hybrid working suits people who manage themselves well.

An interest in broadcast, media or technology is a genuine advantage. The industry has its own language and culture, and the quicker you pick that up, the better you’ll do.

Comfort with ambiguity. We’re a specialist team, not a process factory.

Comfortable using modern tools (including AI) to work efficiently and stay organised.

We’re also a Mac-based team, so familiarity with Apple products is useful.


What We Offer

A base salary that reflects experience, plus an uncapped commission structure designed to reward performance early - not just tenure.

25 days holiday plus bank holidays.

Hybrid working (typically 2–3 days in our Bicester office).

Laptop and phone provided.

Structured onboarding and ongoing development, with direct access to senior consultants who’ve spent their careers in the industry.

A clear progression path - we’d rather promote from within than hire from outside.

The chance to work on assignments for some of the most recognisable names in UK and international broadcast.


A Final Note

This probably isn’t the right role if you’re looking for a heavily scripted, high-volume environment.

But if you want to build real expertise in a specialist market, work closely with experienced consultants, and play a meaningful role in delivering for clients from day one, this could be a strong fit.

If that sounds like the kind of environment you’d thrive in, we’d like to hear from you.

  • Liaising with contractors, the Health and Safety team and the Head of Estates to ensure office audits and any associated works are delivered effectively.
  • Training and support to carry out and then ensure delivery of daily health and safety duties including conducting reviews and supporting the promotion and delivery of first aid and fire safety awareness and training.
  • Assisting the team with the production of any letters, presentations, or other documentation as directed.
  • Assisting with the Office Induction process for new starters based at the development offices and for colleagues visiting from other sites and offices.
  • Liaising with contractors to carry out services including cleaners, security, IT, AV, printers, maintenance etc.
  • Researching tasks and project support as directed.

Community Facilities Co-ordination


  • Liaising across the Sports Hall, Studio, Community Rooms and Community Hub to ensure the venues operate effectively including managing the booking system, liaising with users and arranging equipment and any repairs or services required, supporting invoice and payment collection.

Role Requirements

Urban&Civic is a purpose‑driven company dedicated to shaping thriving communities and creating long‑lasting impact. We’re proud of our collaborative, people‑first culture and our passion for placemaking, innovation and doing the right thing. jobs.title: Head of Operations
jobs.description:
Job Description

Job Description

Role Title: Head of Housing

Organisation: Community Interest Company (CIC)

Reports To: CEO / Managing Director

Direct Reports: Housing Managers / Officers / Support Leads

Role Purpose

The Head of Housing is responsible for leading and developing the organisation’s housing provision, ensuring safe, compliant, and high-quality accommodation aligned with the CIC’s social mission.

This role ensures that housing services are not only operationally effective but also contribute to positive outcomes for residents, particularly those with complex or supported needs.

The postholder will oversee housing strategy, compliance, property standards, and service delivery while ensuring alignment between housing provision and support services.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Develop and implement the organisation’s housing strategy in line with its social impact objectives.

Scale and improve housing provision while maintaining quality and compliance.

Identify opportunities for growth, partnerships, and new housing models.

Provide leadership across housing and accommodation services.

Housing Operations

Oversee day-to-day housing operations across all properties.

Ensure effective allocation, void management, and tenancy sustainment.

Monitor occupancy levels, rent collection, and financial performance of housing stock.

Ensure housing services are responsive, resident-focused, and outcome-driven.

Compliance & Regulation

Ensure full compliance with housing regulations, safeguarding requirements, and local authority standards.

Oversee property compliance including:

  • Health & Safety
  • Fire safety
  • Gas, electrical, and maintenance standards

Maintain robust audit trails and documentation.

Act as the responsible lead for housing-related inspections and regulatory engagement.

Property & Asset Management

Oversee maintenance, repairs, and asset management strategies.

Ensure properties are safe, fit for purpose, and aligned with resident needs.

Work with contractors and landlords to maintain standards.

Support acquisition or onboarding of new properties.

Resident Outcomes & Safeguarding

Ensure housing environments support resident wellbeing, stability, and independence.

Work closely with support/service teams to align housing with care delivery.

Oversee safeguarding processes within housing environments.

Ensure appropriate placement matching (critical in supported housing settings).

Team Leadership

Lead, manage, and develop housing staff.

Set clear performance expectations and accountability.

Build a culture of professionalism, responsiveness, and quality.

Stakeholder Management

Develop and maintain relationships with:

  • Local authorities
  • Commissioners
  • Landlords
  • Regulators
  • Community partners

Represent the organisation in housing-related forums and partnerships.

Financial Oversight

Manage housing budgets and ensure financial sustainability.

Oversee rent setting, service charges, and cost control.

Identify risks related to arrears, voids, or underperformance.

Key Skills & Experience

Essential


Significant experience in housing management, ideally within supported or social housing.

Strong understanding of housing legislation, compliance, and regulatory frameworks.

Experience managing multi-site housing operations.

Proven leadership and team management experience.

Strong understanding of safeguarding within housing environments.

Ability to manage both operational detail and strategic direction.

Desirable

A leading crypto-native algorithmic trading firm is looking for a C++ Trading Platform Developer to join its London-based team.

Why Apply?

At DWS, you’ll have access to a range of benefits which you can choose from to create a personalised plan unique to your lifestyle. Whether you’re interested in healthcare, company perks, or are thinking about your retirement plan, there’s something for everyone.

  • 30 days’ holiday + bank holidays, with the option to purchase additional days
  • A non-contributory pension scheme, up to 10%
  • Physical and Mental Health Well-Being benefits including (but not limited to) Private Medical Cover, a complimentary GP service and the support of Mental Health First Aiders
  • Family friendly benefits including generous parental leave packages (supporting all variations of family set-ups), to healthcare plans and travel insurance
  • The opportunity to support our CSR strategy which is focused on combatting climate change and achieving greater social justice. You can make donations to our partner organisations or take part in corporate volunteering opportunities in your local communities by providing on hand support.


DWS’ Hybrid Working model in the UK is designed to find the right balance between in-person collaboration and engagement in the office, which is core to our working culture, and working from home. Employees who wish to sign-up to our Hybrid Working model are required to work in the office two days a week, and given the flexibility to work from home for the remaining three.


Some business groups may need you to spend more time in the office, but this will be discussed and made clear as part of your application and interview process. Job Description

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an established project manager to join our fast growing and award-winning agency. Here, you will drive and develop projects and accounts and be fundamental to the business and its continued successes.

About Opinium:

MRS 2021 and 2024 Agency of the Year. Winner of the MRS best place to work award three times, the Drum Best Place to Work 2018 & 2019, and the 2019 Women in Research Best Agency to Work Globally. Opinium is a strategic insight agency, that truly puts its people at the centre of everything they do.

Across our four offices in London, New York, Amsterdam and Cape Town, we help our clients harness the power of insight on a global scale to build, grow, promote and make strategic business decisions. We also use Opinium for good, working with multiple charities and volunteering.



Our culture:

We really believe we have a unique culture which provides a stimulating, challenging and rewarding workplace whilst providing a supportive environment and focus on the wellbeing of our people.

“When measuring success, revenue growth and employee wellbeing should go hand-in-hand. It’s the only way to build an insight agency that clients want to work with. We’ve placed our people where they rightfully belong: at the heart of our business.”

Opinium CEO, Chair Market Research Society (MRS)



Your opportunity:

To support our ambitious growth plans, we are seeking to expand Opinium’s Project Management Team. This is an extremely exciting and important move for Opinium, as the project management function acts as a catalyst for the wider research and operations teams.

While Opinium has research team’s based in London, Amsterdam and New York, the project management team only sits within London. This role would be to work as part of Opinium’s Project Management team, working on projects directly supporting our US office, based in NYC.

The team in NYC has seen tremendous recent growth and is in need of an expert project manager to help establish and drive efficient project management operations. You will be the first project manager directly supporting the US team, and would thus have a lead role in driving major team-wide AND company-wide initiatives that drive growth and success.

As part of a very close-knit team, your role will involve working directly with our US office, working closely with their clients and internal teams on multiple projects in parallel. You will oversee the delivery from inception through to final deliverables, ensuring that projects run efficiently, to specification and to budget.

This role would require non-standard UK hours, and would typically be 10:00 AM – 6:30 PM or 10:30 AM to 7:00 PM to support US project work and time zones. These times may be flexible earlier or later based upon daily project needs and agreement with your team or manager as needed. Our goal is to ensure you are part of the London culture, while still supporting the team in the US.

We are looking for people who are passionate, resilient, creative, and authentic. You would value working for a business whilst working on projects for the greater good and building relationships with colleagues and teams.



Role & responsibilities:

Your role is vital to the smooth running of our processes and projects. Here, you will be required to undertake the following core functions:

  • Join key account teams to take responsibility for the end-to-end management of national and international projects, from developing the proposal through to project closure
  • Assess project feasibility, provide costs, and create project plans/timelines for new business proposals and live projects
  • Identify opportunities during the project lifecycle for efficiencies and improvements – both procedural and financial
  • Responsible for maximising financial performance across projects, ensuring costs are minimised where possible
  • Conduct project reviews, assessing the learning and identifying future improvements that could be applied to future projects
  • Act as a point of contact for clients, providing regular updates on project status
  • Grow and manage relationships across Opinium’s partner network
  • Work on wider Operational and Project Management initiatives



Skills and qualities:

Must have skills

We are looking for project managers with around four to five years’ experience within a market research environment. Experience managing qualitative and quantitative projects is essential.

We’re all about passion at Opinium, so successful applicants will show a desire to give it their all, as well as:

  • A proven track record of managing market research projects, both quantitative and qualitative

jobs.title: Senior FPGA Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Description

Join a growing technology company developing advanced sensing and signal processing systems used in demanding real-world environments. The team is expanding its FPGA capability and is looking for a skilled engineer who enjoys working across hardware, firmware, and system-level design.


We are seeking a Senior FPGA Engineer to design and implement FPGA solutions for high-performance signal processing platforms. This role involves working with cutting-edge FPGA technology, contributing to system architecture decisions, and playing an important role in the evolution of the FPGA engineering team.


This position offers strong career progression and the opportunity to take on technical leadership responsibilities as the team continues to grow.


Key Responsibilities


  • Design and develop FPGA solutions for advanced signal processing and sensing systems.
  • Implement and maintain VHDL-based FPGA designs using AMD Xilinx development tools.
  • Develop FPGA architectures targeting Xilinx RFSoC platforms and related technologies.
  • Implement and optimise digital signal processing (DSP) algorithms in FPGA hardware.
  • Develop firmware that interacts with on-chip ARM processors and embedded software environments.
  • Integrate FPGA designs with external DDR memory and high-speed data interfaces.
  • Support the development of multi-clock FPGA systems, ensuring reliable timing and synchronization.
  • Contribute to systems that utilise GPS timing and synchronisation.
  • Collaborate with hardware, software, and system engineers to ensure robust end-to-end solutions.
  • Participate in system architecture discussions, considering peripheral hardware and software integration.
  • Support FPGA verification, debugging, and system bring-up activities.
  • Contribute to mentoring and supporting junior engineers while helping shape the future FPGA team.


Requirements


  • At least 5 years of professional FPGA development experience.
  • Strong experience developing FPGA designs using VHDL.
  • Experience working with AMD Xilinx FPGA platforms and Vivado development tools.
  • Experience with Xilinx RFSoC platforms or Software Defined Radio (SDR) systems.
  • Solid understanding of digital signal processing (DSP) concepts and implementations.
  • Experience integrating FPGA designs with on-chip ARM processors.
  • Experience using external DDR memory within FPGA-based systems.
  • Experience designing multi-clock FPGA systems.
  • Understanding of system-level architecture, including interaction with hardware and software components.
  • Strong problem-solving mindset with the ability to take ownership of technical challenges.
  • Experience working with GPS-based timing or synchronisation systems.
  • Experience developing FPGA systems used in signal processing or sensing applications.
  • Interest in progressing toward technical leadership or team leadership roles.
  • Experience mentoring engineers or guiding technical work.


If your experience aligns with the skills and requirements above, we encourage you to apply now or send your CV to nk@eu-recruit.com.


By applying to this role you understand that we may collect your personal data and store and process it on our systems. For more information please see our Privacy Notice (https://eu-recruit.com/about-us/privacy-notice/)
